calls.reasoning: Deliveries for the closed quarter are known: 486,532 (Model 3/Y 478k, other models 8.3k), with production 22k below deliveries. Splitting Q2 car sales into Model 3/Y (about $40.6k each) and the higher-priced other models (about $80k each) and carrying that to Q3 volumes gives about $20.1B, less about $0.25B of inventory-clearing incentives, so about $19.85B. A year-over-year check at Q3'25's ~$41.0k per delivery gives about $19.95B. Adding credits (~$0.15B), leasing (~$0.35B), energy (~$3.2B at flat storage of 13.7 GWh) and services (~$4.5B, allowing partial reversion of the Q2 jump) gives about $28.1-28.2B. Median $28.25B, slightly below the runs, which added little for discounting or services reversion. Published consensus of $27.7-28.3B may predate the delivery beat. No human market on revenue: the harness found none on Polymarket or Manifold, and earlier traces show Kalshi lists only deliveries. I could not re-check this run.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share identical facts: Q2'26 segment revenue, Q3'26 deliveries and mix, storage, and the consensus snippets. The only factual spread is the earnings date (Oct 20, 21 or 28). It does not affect the value, since the question resolves on the reported figure whenever it is published. The remaining disputes are judgment: how much the inventory drawdown implies discounting, whether the Q2 services jump persists, and energy recognition. My segment and year-over-year builds both land near $28.1-28.2B, so the median is $28.25B, slightly below the runs' $28.35-28.45B. I accept the runs' dispersion of about $1.7-1.85B and the ~1% escape tails on each side (an accounting one-off or restatement would be needed). I had no web access, so nothing was independently verified.
